top_choice_rationale: P003 recognises liquid-liquid phase separation as a thermodynamic organising principle (valency-set phase boundaries, saturation concentration, liquid-like P granules) with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen as the founding observation and its quantitative experimental anchor; a citation held to the principle and not to condensate function rests on the best-confirmed part of the field, and it is a new concept of molecular organisation in living cells. The residual risk is in-cell relevance and the exclusion of Pappu and Mittag. P004 is ranked next because its theory is mature and independent of in-cell evidence; P002 follows as a genuine induced-proximity principle but with a contestable three-name cut and no approved degrader; P001 is mature and cleanly attributed but a ligand-driven sequel to the 2010 cross-coupling prize; a prize of some kind is preferred to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; Lund colleagues Linke and Somfai sit on the committee, but no shortlisted laureate is a known connection, though lipid and membrane phase-behaviour work is adjacent to the condensate field in P003
